explanation: The rule names the two options by one of their labels only ('Match a policy if at least one selected product is supported') and says nothing of what unticking either does, so a rebuilder cannot tell what the filter then does. Also unsaid: ticking 'Supported on' with no product ticked still creates an (empty) product filter, so it does not mean 'no restriction'. The decision is applied in PolicyProcessing.IsPolicySupported (called from Main.vb:432); read it and state each option's on and off effect, and the empty-selection outcome.

Two decisions are merged and the wording is hard to test. Reset applies an empty filter to the whole dialog: type, state and commented go back to Any as well as the product part (lines 22-44, 82-84), and the rule speaks only of products. Split 'opening with no product restriction' (defaults: Supported on unticked, both options ticked) from 'Reset returns every choice to Any'. Lines 21-75 are the decider; the Reset click is evidence.

One rule holds two unrelated decisions in two blocks (Escape cancels, lines 25-27; opening clears the file and prefix boxes, lines 4-6). Split them so each can be checked and owned by the block that decides it. Same pattern for ImportSpol (business rule on ImportSpol.vb lines 28 and 31).

Merges two decisions owned by different blocks: opening clears the earlier result (ImportSpol_Shown, lines 27-29) and Escape cancels unless text is selected in the focused box (ImportSpol_KeyUp, lines 30-32). Its decidedAt cites only line 28 and evidence line 31; the Escape rule should be decided at 30-32. Split into two rules, each at its own block.

The match is the Visual Basic Like operator, which treats more than '*' and '?': '#' matches one digit and '[abc]' / '[!abc]' match a character from a list. For the value name these apply whenever a name is typed (line 21 uses Like unconditionally), so a name holding '#' or '[' is not literal. Say so. Also a malformed pattern (for example an unclosed '[') makes Like throw inside the search; see the missed finding. The same Like reach applies to the key rule at 24-25 (only entered when the key holds '*' or '?').

The wildcard branch is chosen only when the key text contains '*' or '?'; the rule must also say that inside it '#' and '[...]' keep their Like meanings, while a key with only '#' or '[' (no '*' or '?') is treated as a literal path or folder name (lines 26-29). Add that reach.

The rule says a phrase ends at a word that ends with a double quote, but the word that opens the phrase is never tested for a closing quote (lines 42-43 set partialQuotedString and move on; EndsWith is checked only on later words at line 37). So a single quoted word such as "foo" does not form a phrase: it opens one that stays open and swallows the following words until a later word ends with a quote, and if none does it is dropped. Rewrite the split rule with that, and make 'unclosed' (rule 29) include the one-word quoted case. Also words are split on spaces only (Split(text)), and '*'/'?' words inside a quoted phrase are part of the phrase, not wildcards.

The unclosed-phrase case is right, but it misses the common route to it: a quoted single word such as "foo" followed by no later word ending in a quote is also dropped (lines 42-43 never close on the opening word). State that, so a tester can see that searching for "foo" alone matches every policy. 'Every policy that has the searched text' is also vague: with no terms isStringAHit is true for any text, but a policy with no description (Nothing) would fail in cleanupStr rather than match; check what DisplayExplanation can be and word it for title/description/comment separately.

Wildcard words go through Like after cleanup, so '#' still means one digit while '[' and ']' are stripped before the comparison (line 27), so character lists cannot be used here, unlike Find by Registry. Also only spaces, CR and LF split the searched text (not tabs). Add these so the wildcard behaviour can be rebuilt.

Each Find Next advances the remembered position, and the remembered position is also set by Go/double-click at the chosen row (line 123), so Find Next continues after the result the person last went to. The rule says 'the last one chosen' but 'chosen' is undefined; name Go/double-click and Find Next itself as what sets it. It also only walks results listed so far if a search is still running.

Overlaps the rule at lines 96-104 (reopening reselects the last choice and does not search) and its real point is flag housekeeping. The business rule is: reopening never resumes or reruns a search; a search stopped by Stop or by closing stays stopped with the partial results it had. Rewrite to that and drop 'clears the stop flags', or merge it into the reopening rule.

The assumption says case behaviour is not shown, but the lookup tables are plain Dictionary(Of String, ...) built with New and no comparer (PolicyPlus/AdmxBundle.vb lines 11-17, filled at 164-175 with the qualified unique IDs), so the lookup is case-sensitive and the ID must be typed in the exact case. This is a settled rule; write it as a rule on IdTextbox_TextChanged and drop the assumption (read AdmxBundle.vb 11-17 and 160-176 to cite it).

'The others are cleared' is true of policy, category, product and support, but the user/computer section choice (SelectedSection) is never cleared (lines 23-26), so after a policy is found and the text then changes to a category, product, support or no match, the old section is still held. Say so, or note that it only matters when a policy is selected. Also add that the ID is looked up as typed (only surrounding spaces trimmed; case must match).

says: A search function that throws is not handled: Find by Registry's Like on a malformed value or key pattern (for example an unclosed '[' in a value name, FindByRegistry.vb:21,25) throws inside Searcher, which FindResults.SearchJob runs on a background task with no handler (FindResults.vb:47-90,96-98). The likely outcome is that the search stops with no hit, no finishing status and Stop still enabled (the label stays 'Searching...'). Write a rule (or an assumption to confirm in the running system) for what the person sees when the pattern is invalid, owned by FindResults SearchJob and Find by Registry.

Open File in Import SPOL (ButtonOpenFile_Click, no rule written): picking a file replaces the whole text box with the file's contents with no confirmation (unlike Reset, which asks), the picker offers .spol files first and All files, and a cancelled picker changes nothing. Write it as a rule, as was done for the REG file filter.

Search success in Find by Text and Find by Registry has no rule: after the two refusals pass, Search stores the search function and closes the dialog as accepted, which is what makes the results dialog run (FindByText.vb:72; FindByRegistry.vb:36). Add one rule per dialog (or one shared) naming that handoff, as was done for Go in Find by ID.

Whitespace-only text passes Find by Text's 'no text' check (FindByText.vb:13-16 compares to the empty string only), so a text of just spaces produces empty plain words that no policy text contains unless it has doubled spaces. Rule on lines 13-16 should say the check is for empty text, not blank text, and state the outcome of a blank search.
